The options pair organism-named pneumonias, separated by age and onset, with an imaging-phrase mimic (congestive heart failure) and tuberculosis.

edits.html:
Distractors
Unchecked attributePneumonia due to respiratory syncytial virus: it tempts because it is viral and gives diffuse bilateral findings; this virus causes lower respiratory disease with wheeze in infants and children under age 2, not at age 10.
Salient decoyPneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae: it tempts as the most common bacterial pneumonia; it starts abruptly with high fever and a focal lobar consolidation, not a gradual 10-day course with a diffuse film.
Salient decoyCongestive heart failure: it tempts because a diffuse perihilar infiltrate with bilateral crackles also describes pulmonary edema; in children it usually follows congenital heart disease, and this child was previously healthy and febrile.
Unchecked attributeTuberculosis: it tempts because the cough is subacute; there is no exposure, weight loss or night sweats, and the film shows no hilar adenopathy or cavitation.
